anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level runtime settings are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity and workload characteristics.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Database memory structures grow beyond safe physical limits, provoking OS memory pressure and instability.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume an abnormally high share of CPU, driving the host toward sustained core saturation.

When these three root causes co-exist, the system exhibits a tangled symptom set: rapidly rising resident-set size, frequent or continuous paging, and escalating CPU utilisation that remains high even while I/O devices are under-used. Checkpoints, log flushes, or parallel workers may spike suddenly after parameter changes, intensifying run-queue waits and context switching. Cache-hit ratios oscillate as buffer churn collides with swap activity, and query latency becomes erratic—sometimes bound by CPU, other times by stalls on memory allocation or page-in operations. Clustered or virtualised deployments may suffer node eviction or failover storms because watchdog timers expire under the combined memory and CPU stress, making the individual anomalies hard to isolate.

Causally, mis-set configuration parameters (e.g., oversized buffer pools, uncapped work-mem, aggressive parallelism, or overly frequent checkpoints) initiate uncontrolled memory consumption. As physical RAM is exhausted, the operating system starts paging; this not only slows memory access but also forces the database scheduler and background writers to perform extra work, driving CPU utilisation upward. The elevated CPU demand lengthens critical code paths—checkpoint processing, buffer eviction, and memory reclamation—feeding back into both memory pressure and parameter-driven worker proliferation. The positive feedback loop between bad configuration, runaway memory growth, and CPU saturation magnifies each condition, rapidly degrading throughput and stability across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it.
entry.trigger_condition: An interactive session remains idle longer than interactive_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the idle interactive connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
